## 6.2 Database Design

### 6.2.1 Applicability Determination

**Database Design is not applicable to this system.**

`hao-backprop-test` is a single-process, single-file, stateless Node.js HTTP server. Its entire executable surface is `server.js` — 29 lines, 870 bytes — consisting of one `require` of `express` (`server.js:1`), two configuration literals (`server.js:3-4`), three framework statements (`express()` at line 6, `app.enable('strict routing')` at line 12, `app.listen` at line 26) and two route registrations whose handlers write fixed string literals (`server.js:14-24`). The file exports nothing, holds no state between requests, reads no request input, opens no file and connects to no datastore. The three other JavaScript files at the repository root (`Test.test..js`, `!@#$%^&().js` and the 170-character-named `…_server.js`) are byte-identical native-`http` fixtures (md5 `05576d40ab8d9f141d1073f784b26e1b`) that the service never loads.

Because no business data is processed and no data is persisted, none of this section's subject matter has a counterpart in the system: there are no entities to model, no relations to index or partition, no store to replicate or back up, no data lifecycle to migrate, archive or retain, and no database tier to tune. This section therefore states the determination, records the evidence that fixes it, and then disposes of each area the section prompt names — §6.2.2 through §6.2.5 record every required topic as **verified absent**, and §6.2.6 supplies the required diagrams as null-topology views that show the absent tiers rather than an empty schema.

| Required topic cluster | Determination | Documented in |
|------------------------|---------------|---------------|
| Schema design — entity relationships, data models, indexing, partitioning, replication, backup | Not applicable — no datastore, no schema, no records | §6.2.2 |
| Data management — migrations, versioning, archival, storage and retrieval, caching | Not applicable at the data tier; repository and dependency versioning are the only versioning | §6.2.3 |
| Compliance — retention, backup and fault tolerance, privacy, audit, access control | Not applicable — no record is created, retained or disclosed at runtime | §6.2.4 |
| Performance optimization — query optimization, caching, pooling, read/write splitting, batching | No data tier exists to optimize; the request path performs no I/O beyond the socket | §6.2.5 |
| Required diagrams — schema, data flow, replication architecture | Supplied as null-topology diagrams with the persistence and replication tiers marked absent | §6.2.6 |

#### 6.2.1.1 Basis of the Determination

Five independently verified facts carry the verdict. Each is restated with the evidence it rests on, because the same reasoning recurs in the sub-sections that follow.

1. **No datastore client exists in the declared or installed dependency graph.** `package.json:11-13` declares exactly one dependency, `express ^5.2.1`; the root `""` entry of `package-lock.json` mirrors that single declaration, and the 66 non-root package entries that follow are the Express 5.2.1 closure (accepts, body-parser, cookie, cookie-signature, qs, router, send, serve-static and their transitive dependencies). A case-insensitive scan of `package-lock.json` for `sequelize`, `mongoose`, `mongodb`, `postgres`, `pg`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `sqlite`, `mssql`, `cassandra`, `redis`, `memcached`, `prisma`, `knex`, `typeorm`, `level`, `rocksdb`, `aws-sdk`, `database` and `pool` returns zero matches, and the installed `node_modules/` tree matches the lockfile entry for entry.
2. **The complete `require()` surface outside `node_modules/` is four calls, none capable of opening a data connection.** `server.js:1` requires `express`; line 1 of each of the three fixtures requires the built-in `http`.
3. **No storage, filesystem or configuration API is used by any repository file.** A repository-wide scan of every `.js` file returns no `require('fs'|'path'|'net'|'dns'|'cluster'|'worker_threads'|'child_process'|'https'|'crypto')`, no `readFile`, `writeFile` or `createReadStream`, no `fetch`, `axios`, `XMLHttpRequest` or client storage API, and no `process.env` read. No DSN, connection string or credential literal appears in any of the 19 tracked files.
4. **No state is retained between requests, and none is handed to a client.** Both handlers ignore `req` entirely. Measured at HEAD on Node v22.23.3, a request to `GET /` carrying `Cookie: session=abc; user=1`, `Authorization: Bearer x` and the query string `?q=1` returned the same `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/plain`, `Content-Length: 14`, body `Hello, World!\n` as an anonymous request, and no response in the probe carried `Set-Cookie`, `Cache-Control`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified` or `Vary`. The process's only resident state — the Express application object, its two route layers and the listening socket — is discarded at exit (`server.js:6-28`).
5. **No schema, migration, index, backup or configuration artifact exists in the tree.** The repository holds no `.sql` file, no `migrations/`, `db/`, `models/`, `schema/`, `seeds/` or `prisma/` directory, no `.env`, compose file, orchestration manifest, infrastructure template or backup job. The only tracked non-source data file, `phonenumber.csv` (621 bytes: header `message,phonenumber` plus 15 synthetic rows), is read by no code — its name appears only in documentation prose. The Git history holds 11 commits and records no file deletion (`git log --diff-filter=D` is empty), so no removed schema or migration artifact exists in history either.

#### 6.2.1.2 What Persists, and What Does Not

Nothing about this system is stored at runtime, but the repository itself does persist artifacts. The table separates the two, because the distinction is the whole of the data story here.

| Artifact | Where it lives | Runtime role |
|----------|----------------|--------------|
| `server.js` | Git-tracked file, 870 bytes | The entire service; reads no input and writes two literal responses |
| `package.json`, `package-lock.json` | Git-tracked manifests | Read by the npm client at install time only, never by the running process |
| `node_modules/` | Working tree, git-ignored by `.gitignore` | Loaded into memory at `require` time; nothing is written back to it |
| `phonenumber.csv` | Git-tracked fixture, 621 bytes | None — no executable code path opens or parses it |
| Request and response data | Nowhere | Never stored: no file write, no cache, no session store, no request log |
| Process state | Memory only | The Express app object, two route layers and one listening socket; gone at exit |

#### 6.2.1.3 Determinants That Would Otherwise Have Created a Database Design

Every point at which persistence could have entered the design was closed deliberately, and each closure is visible in the tree. The manifests, the published contract and the repository's own requirement notes and remediation plans all constrain the surface in the same direction.

| Determinant | State in this repository | Evidence |
|-------------|--------------------------|----------|
| Storage dependency | One declared dependency, none of it data-tier; 66 installed packages, all framework internals | `package.json:11-13`; `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Configuration surface | Host and port are `const` literals; no `process.env` read, no config file, no CLI argument, no `.env` | `server.js:3-4`; §2.4.1 |
| File I/O | No filesystem module imported anywhere; the only output is a single startup line on standard output | repository-wide scan; §3.5.4 |
| Data fixture | `phonenumber.csv` is present but referenced by no code, so it defines no runtime model | `phonenumber.csv`; §3.5.4 |
| Request-derived state | Handlers accept `req` and never read it; response bodies are compile-time literals | `server.js:14-24`; §5.2.3 |
| Planned hardening | F-101–F-106 improve error visibility and shutdown hygiene only, and forbid adding dependencies; the plan records "No database in use" and a placeholder cleanup comment for future use | `Response.txt` §0.4, §0.5 |

#### 6.2.1.4 Conflict With the Repository's Earlier Verdict

The repository already carries a `6.2 Database Design` section of its own — `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` lines 3114-3450 — which reaches the same "not applicable" verdict, and that verdict is upheld here. Its supporting basis, however, describes a state the repository has since left: that document characterises the system as a 15-line, native-`http` server with **zero** npm dependencies and a lockfile holding only a root self-reference (its §6.2.1, §6.2.1.1), whereas the tree at HEAD runs Express 5.2.1 over a 66-package dependency tree with two registered routes.

Every storage-specific claim in that earlier section that does not depend on the framework was re-verified independently against the current tree and holds: no driver import, no connection string, no `fs` usage, `phonenumber.csv` unloaded, no caching tier at any level, no audit record, and no data-tier access control. What no longer holds is the frame around them — the zero-dependency posture and the single-`require` source that its §6.2.1.1 and §6.2.1.2 rest on. The verdict survives the re-platform because its reasons do not depend on the framework: the system still processes no business data, persists nothing and owns no store.

Two artifacts in the root were examined and set aside as evidence about this system: `tech_spec.pdf` is a 68-page specification for a different project (`existing_project_2511_lakshya_github_5`, dated 2025-11-25) per §6.1.7.1, and `defect_for_task_1.docx` carries 115 characters of unrelated defect text with no occurrence of `database`, `persist`, `storage`, `cache`, `migration`, `SQL` or `schema`.


### 6.2.2 Schema Design

Each schema-design concern the section prompt names is addressed below in turn. All six resolve to **verified absent** for the same reason: the system defines no persisted data, so there is no schema on which an entity, index, partition, replica or backup could be defined. The evidence for each is recorded separately so a reviewer can see that the absence is a property of the code rather than an omission from the design.

#### 6.2.2.1 Entity Relationships

No entity, table, collection or document exists anywhere in the system, and therefore no relationship between entities exists either. The request path constructs no domain object and no transfer object: the handlers at `server.js:14-24` receive `req` and never read it — no header, no query parameter, no path segment, no body — and write one of two compile-time literals. Nothing in the application opens a file, so the one data-bearing artifact in the tree cannot become an entity either: `phonenumber.csv` is byte-present but code-absent, referenced only by documentation prose (§3.5.4, §6.2.1.1).

| Schema concept | Disposition | Evidence |
|----------------|-------------|----------|
| Logical data model | None — no entity or attribute is defined in any file | `server.js:14-24`; `.gitignore`; §3.5.2 |
| Physical data model | None — no table, collection, document or column definition exists | `package.json:11-13`; `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Entity-relationship diagram | Empty — no entity to draw and no relationship to join two | `phonenumber.csv`; §6.2.6.2 |
| Data dictionary | None — no field is declared, typed or documented as data | `server.js`; §3.5.4 |
| Primary, foreign or unique keys | None — no relation exists to key | `phonenumber.csv`; §6.2.2.3 |

The only column-shaped contract in the repository is the orphan fixture's header row, and it participates in no read, write or validation operation:

| Fixture | Fields (from the header row) | Rows | Consumed by |
|---------|------------------------------|------|-------------|
| `phonenumber.csv` | `message`, `phonenumber` | 15 synthetic rows | No code path — the name appears only in prose |

Because the fixture is loaded by nothing, treating it as the system's data model would misstate the system: removing it changes neither startup nor any response.

#### 6.2.2.2 Data Models and Structures

The structures the system actually holds are all transient and all defined in source, not in storage. They are catalogued here because they are the only "models" the system has.

| Structure | Definition site | Lifetime |
|-----------|-----------------|----------|
| Configuration constants | `hostname = '127.0.0.1'`, `port = 3000` (`server.js:3-4`) | Read once at listen time, held for the process's life |
| Application container | `const app = express()` with `strict routing` enabled (`server.js:6, 12`) | In-memory for the process's life; discarded at exit |
| Route table | Two literal `GET` layers, `/` and `/good-evening` (`server.js:14, 20`) | Registered once at startup; a fixed lookup structure (§6.1.2.2) |
| Response payloads | `'Hello, World!\n'` (14 bytes) and `'Good evening'` (12 bytes) | Compile-time literals; recreated per response, never stored |
| Listening socket | `app.listen(port, hostname, callback)` (`server.js:26-28`) | The process's single TCP endpoint on `127.0.0.1:3000` |
| Dependency tree | `node_modules/`, 66 packages resolved from `package-lock.json` | Materialised once per checkout; loaded at `require` time |

There is no record type, no aggregate, no entity identifier, no timestamp field and no schema version field, because no structure outlives the process. The nearest thing to a persisted record set — the 15 fixture rows — is inert: no statement in any repository file reads `message` or `phonenumber`.

#### 6.2.2.3 Indexing Strategy

No index exists, in any form, at any tier. Indexes accelerate lookups against stored relations; this system stores no relations and issues no lookup. What the runtime does hold is one small lookup structure — the two-layer route table — and it is matched by literal path equality under the `strict routing` setting, so its cost is a scan of two entries rather than a tree traversal (§6.1.3.3).

| Index class | Disposition | Evidence |
|-------------|-------------|----------|
| Primary key / clustered index | None — no relation to key | §6.2.2.1 |
| Secondary, composite, unique or covering index | None — no columns and no query planner | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Full-text, spatial or inverted index | None — no text corpus or geometry is stored | `server.js`; §3.5.4 |
| Application-side lookup structure | The fixed two-entry route table, matched on literal path | `server.js:12-24`; §6.1.3.3 |

Nor are any constraints declared or enforced: there is no primary, foreign, unique, check or not-null constraint anywhere, no referential-integrity rule and no cascade behaviour, because no relation exists to carry one. The constraints the repository does carry are build- and contract-level rather than database-level, and they are the only integrity mechanisms in the project:

| Constraint | Where declared | What it enforces |
|------------|----------------|------------------|
| Dependency range | `package.json:12` — `"express": "^5.2.1"` | Any 5.x release at or above 5.2.1, below 6.0.0 |
| Pinned resolution | `package-lock.json` — exact `version`, registry `resolved` URL, `sha512` `integrity` per package | That `npm ci` reproduces the same 66-package tree byte for byte |
| Node.js baseline | Not declared — `package.json` has no `engines` field | Nothing; Express requires Node.js ≥ 18 but the requirement is unenforced (§2.4.1) |
| CSV column contract | `phonenumber.csv` header row `message,phonenumber` | Nothing at runtime — no code validates or reads it |

#### 6.2.2.4 Partitioning Approach

Partitioning is not applicable: horizontal, vertical, range, list and hash partitioning all distribute rows or documents across storage units, and this system has no rows and no documents to distribute. The only partition-like divisions that exist are infrastructural rather than data-tier — one process per host, one event loop per process, and one git-ignored `node_modules/` tree per checkout — and each is a constraint rather than a distribution strategy: the literal loopback bind at `server.js:3-4` admits one instance per host (§6.1.3.1), and the single-threaded synchronous handler gives no reason to spread work across units (§6.1.3.4).

| Partitioning technique | Disposition | Evidence |
|------------------------|-------------|----------|
| Horizontal partitioning or sharding | Not applicable — no dataset to shard | `server.js:3-4`; §6.1.3.1 |
| Vertical or column partitioning | Not applicable — no relation with columns to split | §6.2.2.1 |
| Range, list or hash partitioning | Not applicable — no key space exists | `phonenumber.csv`; §6.2.2.3 |
| Deployment-tier partition (shard per host) | Not possible as configured — fixed loopback address and fixed port | `server.js:3-4, 26`; §6.1.2.4 |

#### 6.2.2.5 Replication Configuration

No replication is configured, and none is possible: replication requires mutable state to propagate, and the system retains none. Both handlers are pure functions of nothing — they read no request input and hold no state between requests — so no replica could diverge from a primary, and no primary exists to diverge from.

| Replication concern | Status | Evidence |
|---------------------|--------|----------|
| Synchronous or asynchronous primary–replica | Not applicable — no primary, no replica, no change stream | `server.js:14-24`; §5.4.6 |
| Multi-primary / active–active topology | Not applicable — no shared state to converge | §6.2.1.1 |
| Quorum or consensus replication (Raft, Paxos) | Not applicable — nothing to agree on | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Logical, streaming or change-data-capture replication | Not applicable — no source of changes exists | §6.2.4.4 |
| Read-replica fan-out | Not applicable — no read workload against a datastore | §6.2.5.4 |

The only reproducibility mechanism in the project is supply-chain rather than data replication: the lockfile pins each of the 66 packages to an exact version and a `sha512` integrity digest, so `npm ci` reconstitutes an identical dependency tree on any host (§6.1.4.3). Nothing runs automatically to verify or refresh it, and it reproduces code, not state.

#### 6.2.2.6 Backup Architecture

No backup architecture exists, because no backup target exists. There is no data volume, no snapshot job, no dump schedule, no offsite copy, no transaction log and no restore procedure in the repository — no `.sh`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.ini` or `.conf` file is tracked at all. Recovery in this system is reproduction rather than restoration: because the service owns no state, the procedure is to re-obtain the source, reinstall the pinned tree and start the process.

| Backup concern | Status | Evidence |
|----------------|--------|----------|
| Full or incremental backup job | None — no scheduler, no script, no backup destination | repository file inventory; §3.5.4 |
| Point-in-time recovery | Not applicable — no transaction log or write-ahead log | `server.js`; §3.5.4 |
| Offsite / cross-region copy | None — no storage service, SDK or credential exists | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Backup verification or restore drill | None — no backup artifact to verify | `.gitignore`; §6.2.3.3 |
| Recovery point objective (RPO) | Not defined — no state to lose between backups | §6.2.4.1 |
| Recovery time objective (RTO) | Not defined — recovery is a manual restart after `npm ci` (§6.1.4.2) | §3.6.5 |

What does survive a total host loss is the source and its manifest, held in Git (HEAD `fdeac01`), plus the public npm registry that serves the pinned packages; neither is a database backup, and both are external to the running system.


### 6.2.3 Data Management

No data lifecycle exists in this system, so the management procedures that normally accompany one have no subject. Each concern is nevertheless recorded below, together with the mechanism that actually governs the analogous change in this repository — source edits, dependency installs and Git history — so that the absence is documented rather than assumed.

#### 6.2.3.1 Migration Procedures

There are no migration procedures, because there is no schema to migrate and no data to move. The repository contains no `migrations/`, `db/`, `models/`, `schema/`, `seeds/` or `prisma/` directory, no migration script, no schema-version ledger (no `__migrations` table or equivalent) and no migration tooling in `package.json#scripts` — whose only entry is the unmodified `npm init` placeholder, `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1` (`package.json:7`). Schema evolution cannot occur where no schema is defined.

The changes the project does undergo have their own procedures, none of which touches a datastore:

| Change type | Actual procedure | Evidence |
|-------------|------------------|----------|
| Response body, route or configuration | Edit the literal in `server.js`, restart the process; recovery if wrong is `git revert` plus restart | `server.js:3-24`; §6.1.6.2 |
| Dependency addition or upgrade | Edit `package.json#dependencies`, run `npm install` to regenerate the lockfile, reinstall, restart | `package.json:11-13`; §3.6 |
| Fixture data | Edit `phonenumber.csv` directly; no schema check, no loader and no consumer exists | `phonenumber.csv`; §6.2.2.1 |
| Runtime state | No procedure — no state is written, so there is nothing to migrate or roll forward | `server.js:14-24`; §6.2.1.2 |

#### 6.2.3.2 Versioning Strategy

No schema or data versioning exists: there is no schema version table, no embedded `version` column on any record, no migration history and no snapshot lineage. The versioning artifacts the repository does hold are all release- or build-level, and none of them is asserted at runtime.

| Versioning layer | Mechanism | Runtime effect |
|------------------|-----------|----------------|
| Application release | `"version": "1.0.0"` (`package.json:3`) | None — no endpoint, header or log line reports it |
| Change history | Git: 11 commits from `2c280c5 Initial commit` to `fdeac01 Adding Blitzy Build Prompt` | None — the service reads no repository metadata |
| Dependency declaration | Semver range `^5.2.1` (`package.json:12`) | Resolved at install time only |
| Dependency resolution | `lockfileVersion` 3 with exact `version` and `sha512` `integrity` per entry in `package-lock.json` | Pins the 66-package tree that `npm ci` reproduces |
| Data or schema | None — no versioned data artifact exists | Not applicable |

The only version identity the service exposes over the wire is the framework's own: `X-Powered-By: Express`, emitted because `node_modules/express/lib/application.js:94` enables it by default and nothing in the application disables it. It identifies the framework, not the release.

#### 6.2.3.3 Archival Policies

No archival policy exists, because no data accumulates to be aged out. Archival moves records from a primary store to a secondary store once an age or access threshold is crossed; this system has no primary store, no record with a time dimension and no threshold to enforce. Requests are not journalled, responses are not retained and the only durable write in the system's life cycle is the dependency install into the git-ignored `node_modules/` (§6.1.4.3).

| Archival concern | Status | Evidence |
|------------------|--------|----------|
| Age- or access-based tiering | Not applicable — no records carry a timestamp | `server.js`; `phonenumber.csv` |
| Cold or object archive target | None — no storage service, SDK or credential in the tree | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.4 |
| Purge or lifecycle rule | None — nothing is written, so nothing needs expiring | §6.2.4.1 |
| Change history retention | Git history only, 11 commits, no pruning or expiry rule | `git log`; `.gitignore` |

Binary artifacts in the repository root — `20250304165759.mp4`, `s1.png`, `tech_spec.pdf` and `defect_for_task_1.docx` — are unreferenced ballast rather than archived data: no code path opens them, and none of them describes this system's storage behaviour (§6.1.7.1).

#### 6.2.3.4 Data Storage and Retrieval Mechanisms

There is no storage tier to describe, and retrieval is a compile-time constant returned over the socket. The complete mechanism is three synchronous statements per handler using the low-level response API — set the status code, set `Content-Type`, write the literal with `res.end` (`server.js:15-17, 21-23`).

| Storage class | Mechanism in this system | Evidence |
|---------------|--------------------------|----------|
| Persistent datastore | None — no driver, no connection string, no query | `package.json:11-13`; `package-lock.json` |
| File-backed storage | None — no `fs` usage in any repository file; the fixture is unread | repository-wide scan; §3.5.4 |
| Session or cookie state | None — the `cookie@0.7.2` and `cookie-signature@1.2.2` packages are present in the dependency closure but no middleware or handler writes a cookie | `package-lock.json`; runtime probe |
| In-memory cache | None — no cache structure and no retained state between requests | §6.2.3.5 |
| Response retrieval path | Literal lookup in a two-entry route table, then a fixed 14-byte or 12-byte body | `server.js:12-24`; §6.1.3.3 |

Measured at HEAD on Node v22.23.3, the retrieval contract is exactly as compiled: `GET /` answers `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `Content-Type: text/plain`, `Content-Length: 14` and `Hello, World!\n`; `GET /good-evening` answers `200` with `Content-Length: 12` and `Good evening`; an unregistered path or a method with no layer (`POST /`) answers `404` from the framework's terminal responder. No response carries `Set-Cookie`, `Cache-Control`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified` or `Vary`, and the process emits no per-request line on standard output — the only log entry in the entire run is the startup banner `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/` (`server.js:27`).

#### 6.2.3.5 Caching Policies

No caching policy exists at any tier, and none is needed: both response bodies are string literals compiled into the source, so there is no computation to amortize and no value that can become stale.

| Caching tier | Status | Evidence |
|--------------|--------|----------|
| HTTP response caching | Absent — no `Cache-Control`, `Expires`, `Last-Modified` or `Vary` header is ever written | `server.js:14-24`; runtime probe |
| Entity-tag validators | Configured but unreachable — Express defaults to `etag: 'weak'`, yet the handlers call `res.end`, so no validator is generated and no conditional request is served from cache | `node_modules/express/lib/application.js:95`; §3.5.3 |
| In-process cache or memoisation | Absent — no cache structure, no memoisation, no shared state between requests | `server.js`; §6.2.1.2 |
| Distributed cache (Redis, Memcached) | Absent — no client in the 66-package closure | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Edge, proxy or client cache | Absent — the listener binds loopback only and ships no static asset | `server.js:3, 26`; §3.5.3 |

Because nothing is stored, there is also no cache-invalidation problem to solve: no write path exists that could make a cached value wrong, and the only bytes that could be cached are the two constants themselves.


### 6.2.4 Compliance Considerations

No record subject to a regulatory, contractual or internal obligation is created, held or disclosed by this system, so the compliance concerns the section prompt names have no operative surface. Each is recorded below with the evidence that fixes its disposition, distinguishing a control that is absent because nothing requires it from one that is absent and would matter if a datastore were introduced.

#### 6.2.4.1 Data Retention Rules

No retention rule exists, and none is required, because no data is retained. The system creates no record of a request: it logs nothing per request, stores no response, keeps no session and writes no file, so there is no retention period to define, no purge schedule to run and no disposal evidence to produce. The single line the process ever emits — the startup banner at `server.js:27` — is an operational diagnostic on standard output, not a retained record.

| Data class at issue | Retained at runtime? | Where a retention rule would live |
|---------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Request content (headers, path, query, body, client address) | No — never read, never logged, never stored | Not applicable; no record is created (§6.2.4.4) |
| Response content | No — compile-time literals, recreated per response | Not applicable; nothing is persisted (§6.2.3.4) |
| User, account or session data | No — no identity, no session, no cookie emitted | Not applicable; `cookie@0.7.2` is present and unused (§6.2.3.4) |
| Fixture rows (`phonenumber.csv`) | Held in the repository as a checked-in file, read by no code | No policy file exists; retention is whatever the Git repository keeps |

For repository content, retention is a property of version control rather than of a data policy: the fixture and source files persist because they are committed, and the history of 11 commits (`2c280c5` through `fdeac01`) is the only lifecycle record. Nothing expires, and nothing purges.

#### 6.2.4.2 Backup and Fault Tolerance Policies

No backup policy and no fault-tolerance policy exists. There is no process supervisor, restart policy, replica, standby, health probe, drain hook or backup job in the tree, and no error-handling code in any application file — a text search of all four application JavaScript files for `try`, `catch`, `.on(`, `process.on`, `process.exit`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, `clientError`, `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` returns zero matches (§6.1.4). Recovery and tolerance therefore reduce to what the runtime and framework do by default.

| Failure class | Mechanism in force | Effect on stored data |
|---------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| Process killed or signalled | Runtime default disposition — no drain, no cleanup hook | None: no state exists to lose or reconcile (§6.2.2.5) |
| Port 3000 already held | The one-shot `error` listener registered by `app.listen` prints the banner and exits `0` (§6.1.4.5) | None — no data path is involved |
| Malformed HTTP request | Node HTTP parser default; answers `400 Bad Request` and closes | None — nothing is parsed or stored |
| Unregistered path or method | Framework terminal responder returns `404` | None |
| `node_modules/` missing or corrupt | Startup aborts at `server.js:1` with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, exit `1` | None — reinstalled with `npm ci` from the lockfile |
| Host loss | Total outage; no instance elsewhere | None — source and lockfile live in Git and on the registry |

No recovery point objective or recovery time objective is defined anywhere in the repository, and neither is measurable for this system in the conventional sense: there is no stored state, so recovery point is not applicable, and recovery time is whatever it takes an operator to free the port, run `npm ci` if needed, and re-run `node server.js` (§6.1.4.2).

#### 6.2.4.3 Privacy Controls

No personal data is processed, so no privacy control is exercised — but the disposition rests on more than the absence of a schema. The handlers ignore `req` entirely, so no header, path, query parameter, cookie or request body can influence execution or be recorded; the process makes no outbound connection, so no data can be forwarded anywhere; and nothing is written at rest, so no encryption-at-rest control has a subject. The one PII-shaped artifact in the tree is the orphan fixture, whose values are synthetic numbers in the `+111111112xx` range and which no code opens (`phonenumber.csv`; §3.5.4).

| Privacy control | Status | Evidence |
|-----------------|--------|----------|
| Data minimization | Achieved by construction — no field is collected, since request data is never read | `server.js:14-24`; §2.4.1 |
| Encryption at rest | Not applicable — no data is persisted at any tier | §6.2.3.4 |
| Encryption in transit | Absent — plaintext HTTP/1.1 over loopback; no TLS terminator or certificate | `server.js:26`; §3.5.1 |
| Subject access, erasure or portability workflow | Not applicable — no subject data is captured, so no record could be exported or deleted | §6.2.4.1 |
| Log scrubbing or redaction | Not applicable — no per-request log exists to scrub | runtime probe; §6.2.4.4 |
| Network exposure limit | The sole control: the listener binds `'127.0.0.1'` (`server.js:3, 26`), so only processes on the same host can reach it | `server.js:3`; §6.1.2.3 |

#### 6.2.4.4 Audit Mechanisms

No audit mechanism exists. The system produces no auditable event: no data is created, modified or deleted by a request, so there is nothing for an audit trail to record. There is no audit log, no append-only journal, no change-data-capture stream, no transaction log, no database activity monitor and no user attribution, because there is no user identity and no authenticated actor.

| Audit primitive | Status | Evidence |
|-----------------|--------|----------|
| Per-request or access log | None — a full run emits only the startup banner on standard output | `server.js:27`; runtime probe |
| Audit log, ledger or event journal | None — no logging library, no log sink, no file append | `package.json:11-13`; §6.2.3.4 |
| Change data capture | None — no data changes occur and no store exists to capture from | §6.2.2.1 |
| Actor or action attribution | None — no authentication, no session, no client identifier is retained | `server.js:14-24` |
| Tamper-evident or timestamped record | None — the single stdout line is neither timestamped by the application nor persisted | `server.js:27` |

The only change history associated with the system is the Git commit log, which records source edits rather than runtime activity, and the only runtime disclosure is the framework's `X-Powered-By: Express` header (`node_modules/express/lib/application.js:94`) — an information disclosure, not an audit record.

#### 6.2.4.5 Access Controls

No database-level access control exists, and no application-level access control either. There is no role model, grant, row-level security policy, column encryption or masking rule, because no datastore exists to which any of them could attach. There is equally no authentication or authorization logic in the application: no authentication, session or token library appears among the 66 installed packages, no middleware is mounted (no `app.use` call exists in any application file), and both routes are reachable by any local client.

| Access-control layer | Status | Evidence |
|----------------------|--------|----------|
| Database roles, grants, row-level security | Not applicable — no database | `package.json:11-13`; §3.5.1 |
| Application authentication or authorization | Absent — no auth library in the dependency closure, no credential check in either handler | `package-lock.json`; `server.js:14-24` |
| Network access control | Loopback-only binding, `'127.0.0.1'` on port `3000` — the sole mechanism limiting who may connect | `server.js:3-4, 26` |
| Secret or credential management | Absent — no `.env` file, no `process.env` read, no credential literal in any tracked file | repository-wide scan |
| Supply-chain access control | `npm ci` resolves the pinned tree from the public registry; the lockfile's per-package `sha512` `integrity` digests are the only tamper check | `package-lock.json`; `.gitignore` |

The practical boundary is therefore the operating system, not the application: file-system permissions decide who may read `server.js`, `package.json` and the lockfile, host firewalling decides whether anything else on the machine can reach port 3000, and the loopback bind decides that nothing off the host can. Introducing a datastore would not extend this posture — it would create the project's first credential, first connection string and first access-control decision (§6.2.1.3).


### 6.2.5 Performance Optimization

The performance techniques this section normally documents are all techniques for a data tier, and no data tier exists. The disposition below records each one as absent, together with the performance properties the system actually has — which come from subtraction rather than tuning: the handlers read no input, allocate no per-request object graph, issue no query and perform no I/O beyond writing a fixed byte string to an already-open socket.

#### 6.2.5.1 Query Optimization Patterns

No query optimization pattern exists, because no query is ever issued. There is no query language in use, no client library, no prepared-statement cache, no query planner to influence, no statistics to collect and no `EXPLAIN` output to tune against; the request path contains no `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, aggregation or join, and no repository file contains an SQL-like statement at all. The lookup that does occur per request — matching the request path against a two-entry route table under `strict routing` — is a literal comparison of at most two candidates, which §6.1.3.3 records as trivial dispatch cost.

| Optimization concern | Status | Evidence |
|----------------------|--------|----------|
| Query planning, statistics or hint tuning | Not applicable — no query planner or client exists | `package.json:11-13`; §3.5.1 |
| Prepared statements or statement reuse | Not applicable — no statement is ever prepared | `server.js:14-24` |
| Index-driven access paths | Not applicable — no index exists (§6.2.2.3) | `package-lock.json`; §6.2.2.3 |
| Result-set shaping (projection, pagination) | Not applicable — no result set exists | `server.js:14-24` |
| Application-side lookup cost | Fixed scan of two literal route entries | `server.js:12-24`; §6.1.3.3 |

#### 6.2.5.2 Caching Strategy

There is no caching strategy, and no caching opportunity: both response bodies are constants compiled into the source, so there is no computation to cache, no I/O to amortize and no value that can go stale (§6.2.3.5). The tiers a caching strategy would populate are all absent — in-process, distributed, HTTP, proxy and client — and the framework's one relevant default, `etag: 'weak'` at `node_modules/express/lib/application.js:95`, is configured but unreachable because the handlers call `res.end` rather than a response helper, so no validator is ever generated and no conditional request can be answered from cache.

| Caching decision | Disposition | Evidence |
|------------------|-------------|----------|
| Application-level result cache | Not applicable — the "result" is a source literal | `server.js:15-17, 21-23` |
| Distributed cache tier | Absent — no client in the 66-package closure | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| HTTP validator or freshness header | Absent — no `ETag`, `Cache-Control`, `Expires`, `Last-Modified` or `Vary` is emitted | runtime probe; §3.5.3 |
| Cache invalidation policy | Not applicable — no write path exists that could make a cached value wrong | §6.2.2.1 |
| Cost of the work being cached | Negligible — three synchronous statements and a constant-body write per request | `server.js:14-24`; §6.1.3.3 |

#### 6.2.5.3 Connection Pooling

No connection pool exists, because the system holds no outbound connection: there is no database client, no cache client, no broker client and no HTTP client in the application or in its dependency closure, so there is nothing to pool. The only connections involved are inbound client sockets to the single listener, and those are owned and managed by the Node.js HTTP runtime rather than by application code — the application never touches a socket, a pool size, a queue or a timeout.

| Pooling concern | Status | Evidence |
|-----------------|--------|----------|
| Outbound connection pool (database or cache) | Not applicable — no client exists to pool | `package-lock.json`; §3.5.1 |
| Pool sizing, warm-up or exhaustion policy | Absent — nothing to size; no `maxConnections`, backlog or rate limit is configured | `server.js:26-28`; §6.1.3.2 |
| Inbound connection reuse | Runtime-managed keep-alive, observed as `Keep-Alive: timeout=5`; idle sockets are held for 5 s, with 60 s header and 300 s request defaults, none of them set by the application | runtime probe; §6.1.3.3 |
| Lifecycle cleanup on shutdown | Absent — no drain hook and no cleanup function exists | §6.2.4.2 |

#### 6.2.5.4 Read/Write Splitting

Read/write splitting is not applicable: there is no primary to write to, no replica to read from and no read or write traffic against any datastore. The service's entire output is a TCP write of 14 or 12 bytes to the requesting socket, measured at HEAD as `Content-Length: 14` for `GET /` and `Content-Length: 12` for `GET /good-evening`. Nothing in the request path distinguishes a read from a write, and no routing, replica-selection or consistency-lag concern can arise where no datastore is contacted.

| Splitting concern | Status | Evidence |
|-------------------|--------|----------|
| Primary endpoint for writes | Not applicable — no write path exists | `server.js:14-24`; §6.2.3.4 |
| Replica selection for reads | Not applicable — no replica and no read model | §6.2.2.5 |
| Consistency or lag management | Not applicable — no replicated state exists | §6.2.2.5 |
| Load-based routing between nodes | Absent — one process serves every request it accepts | §6.1.2.4 |

#### 6.2.5.5 Batch Processing Approach

No batch processing exists at any layer. There is no bulk insert, no batching middleware, no buffer-and-flush queue, no ETL job, no scheduled task and no broker consumer that could amortize per-row overhead, because the system submits no row and processes one request as one synchronous response. Message batching is likewise absent: no producer or consumer, no topic and no queue appears anywhere in the tree (§5.4.3).

| Batch concern | Status | Evidence |
|---------------|--------|----------|
| Bulk or multi-row write path | Not applicable — no write path exists | `server.js:14-24` |
| Request/response batching | Absent — one response per request, written on the same event-loop tick | `server.js:14-24`; §6.1.3.1 |
| Scheduled or background jobs | Absent — no scheduler, no worker thread, no child process | repository-wide scan; §6.1.3.2 |
| Queue or broker consumer | Absent — no messaging client in the dependency closure | `package-lock.json`; §5.4.3 |

Since the handlers perform no work and read no input, the observed cost of a request is dominated by the HTTP stack and the loopback round trip, and the optimisation ceiling for the current contract has already been reached — there is no application-level cost left to remove (§6.1.3.3, §6.1.3.4).
