# 7. User Interface Design

## 7.1 Applicability Statement

> **No user interface required.**

`hao-backprop-test` defines no user interface. The system is a single-process Express 5.2.1 service whose entire executable surface is the 29-line `server.js`, and every response it produces is either a fixed plain-text string written by a route handler or a framework-generated error document. There is no rendered view, no client-side application, no markup template, no stylesheet, no asset, and no end-user interaction surface in the repository. The conventional User Interface Design dimensions named in this section's prompt — core UI technologies, UI use cases, UI/backend interaction boundaries, UI schemas, screens, user interactions, and visual design considerations — are therefore each disposed of below with an explicit non-applicability finding, so that coverage of every dimension remains auditable.

### 7.1.1 Determination of Non-Applicability

The determination rests on four independent observations, each sufficient on its own:

1. **Media type.** Both application routes respond with `Content-Type: text/plain` — `GET /` (14-byte body `Hello, World!\n`) and `GET /good-evening` (12-byte body `Good evening`). No rendered media type is produced by application code anywhere in the service.
2. **Fixed, non-interactive bodies.** Each handler's body is a hardcoded string literal and each handler ignores its `req` argument entirely (`server.js` lines 14–18 and 20–24). There is no data binding, no interpolation, no escaping step, and no input the response could reflect: a request with `Accept: text/html` still receives `text/plain`.
3. **No UI artifacts.** A sweep of every file outside `node_modules/` and `.git/` found no `.html`, `.htm`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.ejs`, `.pug`, `.hbs`, `.njk`, `.mustache`, `.svg`, `.woff*` or `.ttf` file, and no `views/`, `templates/`, `public/`, `static/`, `assets/`, `client/`, `frontend/`, `components/`, `pages/` or `src/` directory.
4. **The service cannot serve one.** No static-file middleware is registered and no view engine is configured: a repository-wide search finds no `express.static(...)` call, no `app.set('view engine', …)`, and no `app.use(...)` of any kind. Requests for asset-shaped paths (`/style.css`, `/app.js`, `/index.html`, `/favicon.ico`, `/static/x.png`) all return `404`.

Introducing a presentation tier would require new server code plus a new dependency (a template engine, a static root, or a client build chain) and a routable markup contract. Both are outside the recorded scope: §1.3.2.1 excludes request processing, content negotiation, and templating, and §1.3.2.3 states that no integration point is active or planned.

### 7.1.2 The Interfaces the System Actually Exposes

What the system exposes instead of a UI is a small set of programmatic and operator-facing surfaces. None of them renders to a person through a browser, a device shell, or a graphical toolkit.

| Exposed surface | Consumer | Medium and contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | Local HTTP client (`curl`, smoke test, probe) | HTTP/1.1 over loopback; `200 OK`, `text/plain`, 14 bytes `Hello, World!\n` | `server.js` lines 14–18; live probe |
| `GET /good-evening` | Local HTTP client | `200 OK`, `text/plain`, 12 bytes `Good evening`, no trailing newline | `server.js` lines 20–24; live probe |
| `OPTIONS /` | Local HTTP client | `200 OK`, `text/plain`, 9 bytes `GET, HEAD`, `Allow: GET, HEAD`, answered by the router without entering either handler | live probe; spec §5.1.3 (transformation 5) |
| `HEAD /` | Local HTTP client | `200 OK` with headers and no body (method aliased to `GET` by the router) | live probe |
| Unregistered path or method | Local HTTP client | `404 Not Found`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, Express's default error document | live probe; `node_modules/finalhandler/` |
| Startup line | Operator reading the terminal | One unstructured stdout line, `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/`, emitted only after a successful bind | `server.js` line 27 |
| Repository documentation and fixtures | Humans and tooling reading the checkout | Markdown, CSV, and binary files that are read from disk, never served over HTTP | `README.md`, `blitzy/documentation/*`, `phonenumber.csv` |

The system's interaction boundary is therefore **machine-to-machine at the HTTP listener and human-to-console at the terminal**. The spec's own boundary inventory records the corresponding finding: the "Observability output" boundary is a single stdout line, and the "Network" boundary accepts plain HTTP/1.1 from any local process (spec §5.1.1).

### 7.1.3 Cross-References Corroborating the Determination

Four already-written sections of this specification independently describe the system in terms that leave no room for a presentation tier:

| Section | Corroborating statement |
|---|---|
| **1.2 System Overview** | The capability table lists five capabilities — Express application and listener, root greeting route, second greeting route, explicit routing with strict paths, startup observability, and the declared dependency — and adds that the system "has no other capability: no request parsing, no state, no persistence, no background work, no scheduled tasks, and no administrative surface." |
| **1.3 Scope** | §1.3.2.1 excludes body/query/header/cookie handling, content negotiation, templating, and static serving; §1.3.2.4 lists "content negotiation and alternate representations" and "internationalization or localization" among unsupported use cases. |
| **3.2 Frameworks and Libraries** | The repository "has exactly one framework and no supporting libraries of its own"; §3.2.6 records "Web, mobile and desktop frameworks: absent … no front-end source file exists"; §3.2.2 notes that no `app.use` call exists anywhere, leaving the framework's middleware layer unused. |
| **5.1 High-Level Architecture** | The architecture is a "single-process, single-file, stateless, loopback-bound monolith" whose inbound interface is "HTTP/1.1 over loopback TCP `127.0.0.1:3000`"; §5.1.3 states that the handler-to-response transformation involves "no templating, escaping, or serialization step". |

No section of this specification describes a screen, a view, a component library, a design system, or a client-side runtime, and none needs to be revised to accommodate this finding.

## 7.2 Evidence of Absence

The absence of a user interface is verifiable in five independent places: the source code, the observed HTTP contract, the dependency tree, the repository inventory, and the project's own requirements and documentation.

### 7.2.1 Source-Code Evidence

`server.js` is 29 lines (22 non-blank) and contains no rendering construct of any kind. Its complete behaviour is: load Express (line 1), declare `hostname = '127.0.0.1'` and `port = 3000` (lines 3–4), create the application (line 6), enable strict routing (line 12), register two literal `GET` routes (lines 14–18, 20–24), and start the listener (lines 26–28).

| Characteristic | Observed in `server.js` | UI implication |
|---|---|---|
| Response construction | `res.statusCode = 200; res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain'); res.end('<literal>')` — three statements per handler | No view object, no render call, no template lookup, no layout or partial resolution |
| Request usage | `req` is accepted as a parameter and never dereferenced | No UI state, user identity, form data, cookie, or preference can reach a response |
| Routing table | Two literal strings, `/` and `/good-evening`; strict routing enabled at line 12 | No view routes, screen identifiers, deep links, or client-side navigation contract |
| Middleware | No `app.use` call exists in any `.js` file outside `node_modules/` | No static root, body parser, session, cookie, CORS, or compression layer on the request path |
| View engine | No `app.set('view engine', …)`, no `app.engine(…)`, no engine import | No server-side rendering pipeline exists to be invoked |
| Static assets | No `express.static(...)` registration and no asset directory in the checkout | No stylesheet, script, font, or image can be served, so no rendering surface is reachable |
| Console output | One `console.log` in the listen callback (line 27) | The only human-readable output the application authors itself is a diagnostic line |
| File I/O | The `fs` module is not imported | No server-side file is read at request time; nothing is rendered from disk |
| Fixture scripts | `Test.test..js`, `!@#$%^&().js`, and the 170-character `QWYFFGH…_server.js` are 14-line native-`http` servers that answer **every** path with `text/plain` and the greeting | Even the alternate executables in the repository produce plain text only |

The deliberate use of `res.end` rather than Express's `res.send` matters here: `res.send` of a string defaults to `text/html`, so the low-level API is what keeps application responses out of the rendered media type (recorded in `blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md` §0.5.2, line 246).

### 7.2.2 Observed Response-Contract Evidence

Every response the service can emit was exercised on a running instance (`node server.js`, Node v22.23.3, Express 5.2.1, bound `127.0.0.1:3000`):

| Request | Status | `Content-Type` | Body length | Body |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | `200 OK` | `text/plain` | 14 bytes | `Hello, World!\n` (verified with `od -c`) |
| `GET /good-evening` | `200 OK` | `text/plain` | 12 bytes | `Good evening`, no trailing newline |
| `HEAD /` | `200 OK` | `text/plain` | none | none (headers only) |
| `OPTIONS /` | `200 OK` | `text/plain` | 9 bytes | `GET, HEAD` with `Allow: GET, HEAD` |
| `GET /GOOD-EVENING` | `200 OK` | `text/plain` | 12 bytes | Path matching is case-insensitive, so this is the same greeting |
| `GET /` with `Accept: text/html` | `200 OK` | `text/plain` | 14 bytes | Content negotiation is ignored; the request is never inspected |
| `GET /nope`, `GET /hello`, `GET /index.html`, `GET /style.css`, `GET /app.js`, `GET /favicon.ico`, `GET /static/x.png`, `GET /good-evening/`, `POST /` | `404 Not Found` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | 143–152 bytes | Express's default error document |

The `404` responses are the only `text/html` the service can produce, and they are framework boilerplate produced by `finalhandler` — not application markup. The complete body for `GET /nope` is:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Error</title>
</head>
<body>
<pre>Cannot GET /nope</pre>
</body>
</html>
```

That document carries no stylesheet, no script, no image, no navigation, and no application data; the request path is its only dynamic content, and it is accompanied by `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, which forbid the document from loading any resource at all. It is a diagnostic page for a developer or a test assertion, not a screen.

### 7.2.3 Dependency and Toolchain Evidence

`package.json` declares exactly one dependency, `express ^5.2.1`, and no `devDependencies`, `optionalDependencies` or `peerDependencies`. `package-lock.json` (lockfile v3) pins 66 packages — Express 5.2.1 plus 65 transitive packages, all of them Express internals (`accepts`, `body-parser`, `cookie`, `debug`, `escape-html`, `finalhandler`, `mime-types`, `path-to-regexp`, `qs`, `router`, `send`, `serve-static`, `statuses`, `type-is`, and similar). The installed `node_modules/` contains no package matching any UI tool: no React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Preact, Lit, Solid or equivalent framework; no EJS, Pug, Handlebars, Mustache or Nunjucks templating engine; no Sass, Less, PostCSS, Tailwind, styled-components or Emotion styling toolchain; no Webpack, Vite, Rollup, Parcel or esbuild bundler; and no JSDOM or Cheerio DOM library.

Two nuances are worth stating precisely, because both could be mistaken for a UI capability:

- **A static-file facility exists in the framework but is never mounted.** `express` re-exports `serve-static`, and `serve-static@2.2.1` and its `send@1.2.1` and `mime-types@3.0.2` dependencies are installed — but `server.js` never registers `express.static`, so the facility is unreachable, and no directory exists that it could serve even if it were registered. Spec §3.2.6 records these packages as "unmounted framework internals … never execute."
- **No client build step exists.** There is no bundler, transpiler, minifier, or asset pipeline configuration in the repository, which means there is no artefact of a front-end build that could be deployed even if one were authored by hand.

### 7.2.4 Repository-Inventory Evidence

All 19 tracked paths were classified against UI relevance, and `git log --all --name-only` confirms that no UI file has ever been committed in any revision:

| Path | Role | UI-bearing? |
|---|---|---|
| `server.js` | Express service entry point | No |
| `Test.test..js`, `!@#$%^&().js`, `QWYFFGHGHFDDJFDame_…_server.js` | Native-`http` filename-edge-case fixtures (342 bytes each) | No |
| `package.json`, `package-lock.json` | npm manifest and lockfile | No |
| `.gitignore` | Excludes `node_modules/` | No |
| `README.md` | Documents dependency, both endpoints, `404` behaviour, run steps | No |
| `codebase_context (42).md` | Original natural-language requirement | No |
| `Response.txt` | Unimplemented hardening remediation plan (server-side resilience only) | No |
| `phonenumber.csv` | Orphan 16-line `message,phonenumber` fixture; imported by no code | No |
| `blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md`, `Project Guide.md`, `Technical Specifications.md`, `Build Prompt.md` (empty) | Project documentation set | No |
| `s1.png`, `20250304165759.mp4`, `defect_for_task_1.docx`, `tech_spec.pdf` | Unreferenced binary/document artifacts | No |

The four binary artifacts deserve explicit treatment, because they are the only files in the checkout that could be mistaken for interface design material. None is web-renderable and none is referenced by any code path:

| Artifact | Size | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| `s1.png` | 49,680 bytes, PNG 1152×958 RGBA | No markup, stylesheet, route, or document references it; a request for any `.png` path returns `404`; nothing in the repository states its origin or content |
| `20250304165759.mp4` | 5,474,705 bytes | A media file carried verbatim in the root; no code path reads, streams, or serves it |
| `defect_for_task_1.docx` | 326,077 bytes | Its entire extracted text is a three-item bug list for an unrelated product ("Overlapping with header in Event update", "Overlapping of Hindi characters", "Skype link not working in simple play.com") — no screen definition, wireframe, or flow for this system |
| `tech_spec.pdf` | 648,521 bytes, 68 pages | A Blitzy-generated Agent Action Plan (sections 0.1–0.10) for a documentation-only task on an earlier native-`http` state of this project, titled `existing_project_2511_lakshya_github_5`; it defines no screen or component, and its only visually oriented item, "Visual Documentation", concerns Mermaid diagrams for the README |

`blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md` §0.6.2 (line 285) reaches the same conclusion, listing `20250304165759.mp4`, `s1.png`, `defect_for_task_1.docx` and `tech_spec.pdf` as out-of-scope artifacts that "are not referenced by executable code". Spec §1.2.2.2 classifies the same four as "Unreferenced exports/attachments; not consumed by the service."

### 7.2.5 Requirements and Documentation Evidence

- **The originating requirement asks for a programmatic consumer.** `codebase_context (42).md` requests "a nodejs tutorial project that features one end point '/hello' that returns 'Hello world' to the calling HTTP client". "The calling HTTP client" denotes a programmatic caller — `curl`, a smoke test, or an integration probe — not a person using a browser. Spec §1.3.2.4 records the related finding that no machine-readable contract and no versioning scheme exist either; `README.md` prose is the only published description of the contract.
- **The project's own agent plan rules the design-system protocol out.** `blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md` §0.5.3 is titled "User Interface and Design System Compliance" and reads: "**Not applicable.** This feature is a headless backend HTTP server that returns `text/plain` responses; it has no graphical user interface, no front-end components, and no rendered views … the **Design System Alignment Protocol does not apply**, no component/token mapping is produced, and no Figma assets are in scope." The same document states at line 256 that "No file in this plan references a user-provided Figma URL, because none were provided" and at line 312 that "No Figma designs were provided."
- **The validation record substitutes endpoint checks for UI verification.** `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §4 is titled "Runtime Validation & UI Verification" and states: "This is a **headless backend HTTP service** returning `text/plain` — it has **no graphical user interface**, no front-end components, and no rendered views … 'UI verification' is therefore replaced by HTTP-endpoint runtime verification." The checks recorded there are the byte-exact bodies, the `404` cases, and the startup line.
- **The committed earlier specification reached the same verdict.** `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` §7 already carries the "No user interface required" declaration for this repository. That document describes the superseded native-`http`, zero-dependency state — its own §2.7.4 concedes that a change to `server.js` invalidates its acceptance criteria, and spec §1.2.1.2 records the divergence — but its conclusion about the absence of a presentation tier still holds for the current Express implementation, for the reasons given in this section.

## 7.3 Disposition of UI Design Dimensions

The dimensions below are those enumerated by this section's prompt. Each is recorded as non-applicable with its specific evidence, so that a reader auditing coverage can see that the dimension was addressed rather than omitted.

### 7.3.1 Core UI Technologies

**Not applicable.** No UI technology is present in the repository. The complete technology surface is the Node.js runtime (validated on v22.23.3), JavaScript in CommonJS form, the single framework `express@5.2.1`, the Node built-in `http` module used by the fixture scripts, and the `console` global used for one startup line. Spec §3.2 opens with "The repository has exactly one framework and no supporting libraries of its own", and §3.2.6 records that "Web, mobile and desktop frameworks: absent … no front-end source file exists". There is consequently no markup language, no styling system, no rendering engine, no component library, no design system, no client-side runtime, and no server-side template engine.

### 7.3.2 UI Use Cases

**Not applicable.** The system has one operational workflow, and every step of it is a command or an HTTP exchange rather than a screen: install dependencies, start `node server.js`, exercise the two greeting endpoints, observe the `404` rejection, terminate the process (spec §1.3.1.1). Its user groups are "local operators who start the process, local HTTP clients and smoke tests on the same host, and tooling that consumes the repository as a fixture" (spec §1.3.1.2) — none of which is an end user of a user interface. There are therefore no user journeys, screen flows, personas, or task flows to document, and no use case is expressed as a UI interaction. The use cases the specification explicitly excludes include stateful interactions, content negotiation, and internationalization (spec §1.3.2.4), which are the cases most likely to introduce a UI surface.

### 7.3.3 UI / Backend Interaction Boundaries

**Not applicable as a UI boundary.** There is no presentation tier for a UI/backend boundary to sit between; the only boundary of any kind is the loopback HTTP listener. Its properties are as follows.

| Property of the sole boundary | Observed value |
|---|---|
| Address and protocol | `127.0.0.1:3000`, HTTP/1.1 plaintext, keep-alive enabled (`Keep-Alive: timeout=5`) |
| Reachability | Loopback only — any local process can reach it, no host off the machine can |
| Authentication, sessions, cookies | None; no CORS, TLS, or authorization layer exists |
| Request data that affects a response | The method and the request path only; headers, bodies, query strings and cookies are never read, and content negotiation is ignored |
| Response payloads | Fixed literals (14 bytes on `/`, 12 bytes on `/good-evening`) or the framework's fixed-length diagnostic document |
| Non-HTTP interfaces | None — no JSON API, RPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, server-sent events, or file upload surface |

Spec §5.1.1 records the same boundary as "HTTP/1.1 over loopback TCP `127.0.0.1:3000`" with "no TLS, no authentication, no client filtering", and states explicitly that what lies outside it includes "no metrics or tracing backend, no administrative or health endpoint". Spec §5.1.3 traces the per-request flow from the socket through `app.handle`, the router and a handler, and notes that no request-derived value is retained, logged, forwarded, or stored.

### 7.3.4 UI Schemas

**Not applicable.** A UI schema would describe view models, form fields, component properties, or a data binding between a service contract and a rendered element. None exists, because the service has no structured contract to bind to: both responses are opaque fixed strings, and the only structured media type it can emit is the framework's error document, whose sole dynamic value is the request path. There is no JSON, XML, or problem-details payload; no query or body parameter; and no machine-readable API description — spec §1.3.2.4 records that "no versioning scheme, deprecation policy, or machine-readable contract (for example OpenAPI) exists", leaving `README.md` prose as the published contract.

The repository does contain one data schema, and it is bound to nothing: `phonenumber.csv` is a 16-line file with the header `message,phonenumber` and 15 synthetic rows using numbers in the `+111111112xx` range. It is imported by no executable code, served by no route, and mapped to no view, so it cannot be described as a UI schema in any sense.

### 7.3.5 Screens Required

**Not applicable.** No screen, view, page, panel, dialog, modal, drawer, or popover is required, defined, or implemented, and no file or directory exists that could host a screen definition (see 7.2.4). The only document-shaped artefact any code path in the repository can produce is the framework's `404` error page shown in 7.2.2, which contains no application markup, references no asset, and is served with `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`, so it cannot load the resources a rendered interface would need. The three native-`http` fixture scripts answer every path with plain text and therefore also cannot produce a page.

Were a screen ever required, it would need server code plus a new dependency or a static root (spec §1.3.2.1 excludes templating and static serving; §1.3.2.2 lists the only candidate future phases — server-side hardening and the unimplemented `/hello` endpoint — and neither introduces a presentation surface).

### 7.3.6 User Interactions

**Not applicable.** The system never interacts with a person through a control, a form, or a rendered element. Its interactions are:

- **HTTP request/response with a client** — machine-to-machine over loopback. The only client-perceptible distinctions are `200` versus `404`, case-insensitive path matching (`GET /GOOD-EVENING` succeeds), the significance of a trailing slash (`/good-evening/` is `404`), and the `Allow: GET, HEAD` advertisement returned for `OPTIONS /`.
- **One startup line to standard output** — write-only, emitted once per process, carrying no interactivity.
- **Signal-driven termination** — `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` reach the process through the operating system with the runtime's default disposition and no application handler (spec §5.1.1, §5.1.4).

None of these presents input affordances, validation feedback, navigation, loading states, or error states to a user; the failure modes are HTTP status codes and a terminal line.

### 7.3.7 Visual Design Considerations

**Not applicable.** There is no visual design to specify and none was requested. Specifically absent from the repository: design tokens; colour palettes; typography scales; spacing systems; layout grids; iconography; imagery; responsive breakpoints; animation or transition specifications; theming (light/dark); accessibility provisions such as WCAG conformance levels, ARIA roles, focus management, or contrast requirements; internationalization or localization resource files; and brand guidelines. The supporting evidence is that no stylesheet, font, icon, or image asset exists in the checkout; that no Figma reference exists — `blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md` records at line 256 that no user-provided Figma URL was supplied and at line 312 that "No Figma designs were provided"; and that response bodies are fixed ASCII English text with `Accept-Language` never consulted.

The only legibility considerations that arise at all belong to the two non-UI surfaces: the startup line is plain uncoloured ASCII emitted to a terminal, and the framework error document is a minimal HTML page that renders its message inside a `<pre>` element. Both are framework or runtime defaults rather than a designed presentation layer, and neither is a design-system concern.

## 7.4 Operator-Facing and Diagnostic Surfaces

Two non-UI surfaces carry information to a person, and both are worth recording so that no reader mistakes them for an interface.

| Surface | Audience | What it delivers | Why it is not a user interface |
|---|---|---|---|
| Startup line on stdout (`server.js` line 27) | Operator or log consumer at the terminal | The single line `Server running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/`, emitted once per process after a successful bind | Write-only, unstructured, untimestamped, unlevelled; emits no per-request logging and accepts no input. Spec §5.1.4 also records that if the bind fails the same success line has already been printed and the process then exits `0` with no diagnostic, so the line is a coarse signal rather than a control surface |
| Terminal rendering of an HTTP response | Developer or test harness invoking `curl` | The two greeting bodies verbatim, or the `404` status when a path is unregistered | The bytes are produced by a programmatic client's own rendering of a `text/plain` payload; the service neither formats nor styles them |
| Framework error document | Developer or test assertion | The `text/html; charset=utf-8` page shown in 7.2.2, with the request path echoed inside `<pre>` | Generated by `finalhandler`, not by application code; contains no navigation, data, or assets, and forbids resource loading through `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` |

The same picture holds for the whole request path: a client may be a browser — a browser can open `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` and will display the plain-text bytes — but no code in this repository produces a document for that browser to lay out, and no route exists that could serve one.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client["Local HTTP client<br/>curl / smoke test / browser"] 
    Operator["Operator terminal<br/>reads stdout"]

    subgraph Process["Single Node.js process — server.js"]
        App["Express 5.2.1 application<br/>two literal GET routes"]
        Handler["Greeting handlers<br/>res.end fixed literals"]
        Final["finalhandler 2.1.1<br/>framework error document"]
        Log["console.log<br/>startup line"]
    end

    subgraph Absent["Presentation tier — absent from this repository"]
        BrowserShell["Browser rendering surface"]
        Screen["Screen, view or page"]
        Renderer["Template engine or client framework"]
        Tokens["Design tokens, stylesheets, assets"]
    end

    Client -->|"GET / , GET /good-evening"| App
    Client -->|"unregistered path or method"| Final
    App --> Handler
    Handler -->|"200 text/plain, 14 or 12 bytes"| Client
    Final -->|"404 text/html diagnostic page"| Client
    Log -->|"one line on stdout"| Operator
    Client -.->|"no document is produced"| BrowserShell
    BrowserShell -.->|"no view is ever served"| Screen
    Renderer -.->|"not installed"| Screen
    Tokens -.->|"no asset exists"| Screen
```

Every edge into the "Presentation tier" subgraph is dashed because those nodes are reached by nothing: the service has no view, no asset, and no template to hand to a rendering surface.

## 7.5 Summary

The User Interface Design dimension of `hao-backprop-test` is formally **not applicable**, and the required note — **no user interface required** — is recorded at 7.1. The determination is supported from five directions: the source code contains no rendering construct (`server.js`), the observed HTTP contract carries only `text/plain` bodies plus a framework-generated error document, the dependency tree holds a single framework with no UI package of any kind, the repository inventory contains no UI file or directory and never has (including the four unreferenced binary artifacts), and the project's own requirements and documentation — from the originating ask in `codebase_context (42).md` to `Agent Action Plan.md` §0.5.3 and `Project Guide.md` §4 — describe a headless backend service and explicitly rule the design-system protocol out.

Consequences for the rest of this specification:

- **No other section requires amendment.** Sections 1.2, 1.3, 3.2 and 5.1 already describe a system with no presentation tier, and their statements remain accurate and sufficient.
- **The system's human-facing surface is limited to output.** One startup stdout line, the text a client renders from a `text/plain` body, and the framework's diagnostic `404` page are the only things a person can see; none of them accepts input, and none is authored as an interface.
- **A future UI would be a scope expansion, not a refinement.** Delivering one would require new server code, a new dependency (a template engine, a static root, or a client build chain), and a routable markup contract, none of which appears in the recorded in-scope set or in the future phases catalogued in spec §1.3.2.2. Such a change would invalidate the acceptance conditions here and require a new revision of this specification.

# 8. Infrastructure

## 8.1 Applicability Determination

> **Detailed Infrastructure Architecture is not applicable for this system.**

The entire executable surface of `hao-backprop-test` is the 29-line CommonJS file `server.js`: one `require` of `express` (line 1), two `const` configuration literals (lines 3-4), one framework setting (line 12), two `GET` route registrations whose handlers write compile-time string literals (lines 14-24), and one listener that binds the literal loopback address (lines 26-28). "Deployment" is a single operator action on a single host: install the dependency tree from the committed lockfile, then execute the file. The system owns no environment, no cluster, no image, no pipeline, no configuration store, no supervisor and no monitoring agent. §1.3.2.1 records the corresponding exclusions in writing, listing "Clustering, process managers, container definitions, and orchestrator manifests" under Lifecycle and "Automated tests …, linters/formatters, CI pipelines, and type checking" under Tooling.

The conventional motivations that give rise to infrastructure architecture — a production deployment to protect, environments to promote between, tenants to isolate, capacity to plan, a provider bill to optimise, a compliance regime to audit — are absent together with the operating context that would create them (§1.3.1.2; §1.3.2.4). The determination mirrors the precedent this specification already sets for Core Services (§6.1), Database (§6.2), Integration (§6.3), Security (§6.4) and Monitoring (§6.5): the required topic clusters are dispositioned explicitly rather than omitted, and the minimal build and distribution requirements the system does have are documented in §8.2.

### 8.1.1 Basis of the Determination

Ten independently verified facts carry the verdict. Each is stated with the artifact it rests on, because the same reasoning recurs in every sub-section that follows.

| # | Determining fact | Evidence at HEAD |
|---|------------------|------------------|
| 1 | No build step of any kind | `package.json` declares no `build` script, and no bundler, transpiler, task runner or type checker is installed or configured (§3.6.2); the source tree is the artifact |
| 2 | No container definition | A search of the whole checkout for `Dockerfile*`, `docker-compose*`, `.dockerignore`, Helm charts and Kubernetes manifests returns nothing; the only directories outside `node_modules/` and `.git/` are `blitzy/` and `blitzy/documentation/` |
| 3 | No orchestration or process supervision | No orchestrator manifest and no PM2, systemd, forever or nodemon configuration exists; no `cluster` or `worker_threads` reference appears in any repository JavaScript file |
| 4 | No CI/CD | No `.github/` directory exists and no pipeline marker file of any provider is present; the history is 11 commits on one branch, and none of them adds a pipeline |
| 5 | No infrastructure as code | No `.tf` or `.tfvars` file, `Pulumi.yaml`, CloudFormation template, CDK app, Ansible playbook, Chef cookbook or Puppet manifest exists |
| 6 | No cloud services | `npm ls --depth=0` resolves `hello_world@1.0.0 -> express@5.2.1` and nothing else; `package-lock.json` (`lockfileVersion` 3) holds 66 entries, all of them the Express 5.2.1 closure, so no cloud SDK is reachable |
| 7 | No configuration surface | No `.env`, `.conf`, `.cfg`, `.ini`, `.yml`, `.yaml` or `.toml` file exists anywhere, and no `process.env`, `process.argv`, `app.set` or `app.use` reference appears in any repository JavaScript file |
| 8 | No version or platform pin | `package.json` declares no `engines`, `private`, `type` or `os` field, so nothing constrains the runtime, the package manager or the operating system that executes the service |
| 9 | No lifecycle control | The process installs no signal handler and no error handler: measured at HEAD, `SIGTERM` ended it with exit code `143` without draining, and a second instance launched while port 3000 was held printed the success banner, wrote nothing to standard error and exited `0` |
| 10 | No monitoring instrumentation | No APM, metrics, tracing or log-shipping package is installed, and no call site exists in which one could be wired (§6.5.2) |

### 8.1.2 Repository Role Context

`README.md` states the project's role in two lines — `hao-backprop-test`, a "test project for backprop integration" — and `package.json` describes it as "Hello world in Node.js". The artifact is a fixture and a tutorial exercise, not a product: it has no external consumer, no tenant and no audience for a dashboard or an availability commitment. Its single network interface is the listener in `server.js`, bound to `127.0.0.1:3000`, which no other host can reach without infrastructure that §1.3.2.4 explicitly places outside scope. Its single operator is whoever launched the process, and its single runtime dependency in production terms is the public npm registry, reached once at install time (§1.3.1.1).

That role explains the posture rather than merely describing it. The work recorded around the delivered change is equally explicit: `blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md` §0.6.2 scopes testing, linting, CI/CD, containerisation and configuration files out of the delivered work, and the unimplemented hardening plan in `Response.txt` §0.5 forbids adding logging libraries, monitoring instrumentation, health endpoints and metrics to the superseded implementation. No infrastructure capability was omitted by oversight; each was ruled out in writing.
