| Manifests | 35,031 | 0.5% | `package.json` and the 66-package lockfile |
| Runtime code | 1,896 | 0.03% | `server.js` plus the three byte-identical fixtures |
| Configuration | 14 | 0.0002% | `.gitignore`, one rule |
| **Total tracked** | **7,147,208** | **100%** | 19 tracked paths |

The dependency tree sits outside that total: `node_modules/` measures 4.2 MB across 66 packages — 65 directories at its top level plus one nested copy at `node_modules/type-is/node_modules/content-type` — and is reproducible from the lockfile rather than carried in version control. The distribution makes the system's proportions explicit: 0.03% of the tracked content is the code that serves every request, and the remaining 99.97% is manifests, documentation, fixtures and payload the running service never loads.


## 9.2 Glossary

The terms below are those this specification and the repository's own artifacts use with a specific, narrower meaning than ordinary usage. Each definition is stated as the term is used here and is anchored to the artifact or section that fixes it.

### 9.2.1 Delivery, Process and Record Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|------|------------------------------------------|
| Acceptance criterion | A single observable that must be true for a feature to count as delivered, addressed by an `F-xxx-RQ-nnn` identifier (§2.2). None is enforced by a test, because no automated suite exists (§6.6.4.4) |
| Path-to-production | The human review, assumption confirmation, merge and deployment steps that remain after autonomous implementation; the project guide prices them at 1.5 hours (`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §2.2) |
| Change set | The exact set of files a delivered change touches. For this feature it is five: `server.js`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.gitignore` and `README.md` (§9.1.3) |
| Superseded artifact | A repository document that describes an earlier state of the system and no longer governs it. `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` is superseded because it documents the pre-Express, zero-dependency implementation (§2.1, §6.6.1.4) |
| Freshness invalidation | The condition a specification states for its own obsolescence. The superseded specification declares that any modification to `server.js` invalidates its F-001–F-005 acceptance criteria (§2.4.5, §2.5.5) |
| Verified absent | A capability claim stronger than "not implemented": absence established by enumerating every code-bearing file, as §1.3.2.1 does for authentication, TLS, persistence, tests and pipelines |
| Applicability determination | A section-level decision that a required topic cluster has nothing to document on this system, stated with the evidence and the fallback approach that applies instead (§6.6.1, §8.1) |
| Null topology | A diagram convention used throughout this document: the one edge that exists is drawn solid, and each component a conventional architecture would contain is attached by a dashed edge labelled as verified absent (§6.6.9) |
| Aspirational threshold | A numeric target recorded in `Response.txt` §0.6 for the unimplemented hardening variant — under 50 ms response, under 50 MB RSS, 100+ concurrent connections, a 10-second shutdown guard — and adopted by no part of the delivered system (§5.4.5) |
| Validation register | The project's durable test record: 15 checks in `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §3, of which 9 are functional HTTP-contract checks. It is a record, not a runnable asset, because the harness that produced it is not committed (§6.6.7.1) |
| Test oracle | The artifact a verification pass is written against. Here it is `README.md` lines 4–12, the only published statement of expected behaviour (§6.6.4.5) |
| Golden baseline | A stored expected output used for comparison. The pre-migration `Hello, World!\n` body served this role for the root route, which is why FR-C required it to be preserved byte for byte (§2.1.3.4) |
| Regression protection | An automated assertion that would fail if a verified behaviour changed. None exists for this system: nothing runs on commit, push or merge (§6.6.7.5) |
| Deferred enhancement | An improvement the project deliberately left out of the delivered change and recorded as optional, with an effort estimate: a regression suite (~2.0 h), `X-Powered-By` suppression (~0.25 h), and host/port parameterisation (~1.0 h) (§2.4.5, §6.6.10.1) |
| Assumption register | The set of unresolved questions the delivering agent flagged rather than decided: the endpoint path `/good-evening`, the absent trailing newline on `Good evening`, and the preserved `Hello, World!` wording (§2.5.5) |
| Record conflict | Two repository records that disagree about the same fact. This specification reports both with their sources and states which governs; §9.1.6 consolidates all ten |
| QA Issue 1 | The one defect found after delivery — `GET /good-evening/` returning content although the trailing-slash variant is unregistered — fixed in commit `f2c2ca4` by enabling strict routing (§6.6.3.3) |
| Traceability matrix | The mapping that links each feature to the requirement that originated it, to the source artifact that evidences it, and to the validation check that exercises it (§2.5) |
| Feature ID | The `F-nnn` identifier that names a capability; retained from the superseded catalogue where a capability survives, and extended with F-007–F-010 and F-201 (§9.1.4) |
| Requirement ID | The `FR-A`–`FR-D` identifier the action plan uses for the delivered change, and the `F-xxx-RQ-nnn` identifier used for individual acceptance criteria (§9.1.4) |

### 9.2.2 Runtime, Protocol and Failure Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|------|------------------------------------------|
| Loopback | The `127.0.0.1` address, reachable only from processes on the same host. It is the system's entire access-control boundary: no authentication, authorisation or TLS exists behind it (§5.4.4) |
| Strict routing | The Express setting enabled at `server.js` line 12 that makes trailing-slash variants distinct paths, so `/good-evening` is registered and `/good-evening/` is not (§3.2.2) |
| Route-agnostic | The pre-migration behaviour in which one handler answered every method on every path; it survives only in the three fixture scripts (§3.2.6) |
| Byte-exact | A response body that matches the specified bytes precisely, including or excluding a trailing newline. It is the reason both handlers call `res.setHeader`/`res.end` rather than `res.send` (§3.2.2) |
| Trailing newline | The distinction between the two contracts: `Hello, World!\n` is 14 bytes, `Good evening` is 12 bytes with no newline (§1.1.1) |
| Keep-alive | Socket reuse for successive requests on one connection. Idle sockets are reaped after 5 seconds, with `headersTimeout` at 60 s and `requestTimeout` at 300 s as runtime defaults (§5.1.1, §5.4.5) |
| Content negotiation | Selecting a representation from a client's `Accept` header. It is not implemented: neither handler reads a request header, and `text/plain` is the only media type on success (§1.3.2.4) |
| Conditional request | A request carrying a validator such as `If-None-Match`, which can produce `304 Not Modified`. No such path exists, because no validator is emitted (§4.3.1.4) |
| ETag | An entity-tag response validator. The framework's `etag` setting is `weak`, but no tag is ever computed, because the handlers bypass `res.send` and emit no `Cache-Control`, `Expires` or `Last-Modified` either (§3.2.3, §5.1.3) |
| `X-Powered-By: Express` | The framework's default disclosure header, present on every response including `404`s. Suppressing it requires `app.disable('x-powered-by')`, which is documented as optional and not implemented (§2.4.4) |
| Default 404 body | The framework refusal rendered by `finalhandler@2.1.1`: `Cannot <METHOD> <path>` as `text/html; charset=utf-8`, with `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (§2.1.3.6) |
| Readiness probe | A signal an external supervisor can poll to decide whether to route traffic. None exists: the only readiness evidence is TCP acceptance on port 3000 and a successful request, since the startup banner also prints when the bind failed (§8.10.3) |
| Structured logging | Log output carrying levels, timestamps and fields. The application emits one unstructured line, without level or timestamp, and no logging library is declared (§5.4.2) |
| Telemetry and APM | Metrics, traces and application performance monitoring. None is emitted: no client library, agent or exporter exists in the 66-package tree (§5.4.1) |
| SLI and SLO | Service-level indicator and objective. Neither is defined anywhere in the repository; the only numeric figures are point-in-time measurements and the aspirational values of an unimplemented variant (§5.4.5) |
| Drain | Letting in-flight requests finish before the process exits. No drain exists: `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` take the runtime's default disposition and end the process immediately (§4.3.2.1, §8.10.2) |
| Graceful shutdown | The proposed but unimplemented F-102 behaviour: handlers for `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` that call `server.close()` with a 10-second force-exit guard (§2.1.4.2) |
| One-shot error listener | The framework's `listen` wiring, which registers the startup callback as the server's `error` listener. It is why a bind conflict prints the success banner, writes no diagnostic and exits `0` (§4.3.2.1, §6.6.2.2) |
| `EADDRINUSE` | The bind error raised when the address and port are already held. In this repository it is fatal only for the fixture scripts; the Express service swallows it (§9.1.6, row 7) |
| `EACCES` | The bind error raised when the process lacks permission for the address or port. It is named as a target of the unimplemented F-101 handler (§2.1.4.1) |
| `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` | The module-loader error raised at `server.js` line 1 when dependencies are absent, producing the message `Cannot find module 'express'` and exit status 1 (§4.3.2.1, row 1) |
| `EBADENGINE` | The npm warning raised when the host runtime does not satisfy a package's declared engine range. It is a warning rather than a refusal, because no `engines` field and no `engine-strict` setting exist (§3.1.3) |
| Exit status | The process-exit code an operator observes: `0` for a clean start and a swallowed bind conflict, `1` for an unresolved dependency or an uncaught exception, `130` on `SIGINT`, `143` on `SIGTERM` (§8.10.2) |
| `NODE_ENV` | The environment variable the framework consults to decide error verbosity. Nothing in the repository sets it, so the effective value is the `development` default and a genuine `5xx` would disclose a stack and filesystem paths (§6.6.5.2) |
| `DEBUG` | The environment variable the transitively installed `debug@4.4.3` package reads. Nothing sets it, so the framework's per-request dispatch and refusal lines stay silent (§5.4.1) |
| RSS | Resident set size, the resident memory an operator measures for the process. It is observed rather than budgeted: approximately 62–64 MB while idle in this checkout (§8.11.2, §8.10.2) |
| `HEAD` | Used in two senses. As an HTTP method it is aliased to the matching `GET` handler, so `HEAD /` returns the root headers; as a git term it names the current commit, which for this checkout is `fdeac01` (§6.6.2.2, §9.1.3) |

### 9.2.3 Framework and Dependency Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|------|------------------------------------------|
| Express application | The object `express()` returns at `server.js` line 6. It owns the settings map and the routing table and is the only request pipeline in the service (§2.1.3.1) |
| Routing table | The two literal `GET` layers registered by `app.get` at lines 14 and 20, held by the framework's router and closed to further change once both registrations have run (§4.3.1.1) |
| Router | The framework's `router@2.2.0` package, which lowercases the method, discards the query string, matches the path case-insensitively and falls through when nothing matches (§5.1.2, component C-2) |
| `finalhandler` | The `finalhandler@2.1.1` package installed as the terminal callback of `app.handle`; it renders the `404` and framework `5xx` responses and logs only when an error object is supplied (§5.1.2, component C-5) |
| Middleware | A function mounted with `app.use` to run before handlers. No such call exists anywhere in the repository, so the entire middleware layer — body parsing, static serving, cookies, compression — is unused even though its packages are installed (§3.2.2, §3.3.2) |
| Express settings | The application's key/value configuration. Only `strict routing` is written by the code; `x-powered-by`, `etag`, `query parser`, `trust proxy`, `env` and `subdomain offset` hold framework defaults that the document treats as observable behaviour (§3.2.3, §4.3.1.1) |
| Router options captured at construction | The framework reads `strict` and `caseSensitive` once, when the router is first built on the first `app.get`. That makes the order of `app.enable('strict routing')` before the route registrations load-bearing (§5.1.2, component C-2) |
| Direct dependency | A package `package.json` declares. The project has exactly one, `express`; Express itself declares 28 (§3.3.1) |
| Transitive dependency | A package pulled in by another dependency rather than declared here: 37 deeper in the graph, producing the 66-package installed tree (§3.3.1) |
| Lockfile | `package-lock.json` at `lockfileVersion` 3, recording 67 `packages` keys — a root entry mirroring the manifest plus 66 package entries, each pinned by exact version, registry URL and `sha512` integrity digest (§3.3.2) |
| `npm ci` versus `npm install` | Only `npm ci` reproduces the committed tree; `npm install` may resolve a newer minor inside the caret range and rewrite the lockfile, which is why the lockfile rather than the manifest guarantees reproducibility (§3.3.1) |
| Caret range | The semver range `^5.2.1`, meaning `>= 5.2.1 < 6.0.0`. It permits an upgrade the lockfile has not taken: 5.3.0 is the current npm `latest` (§3.2.1, §3.3.1) |
| Integrity digest | The `sha512-…` Subresource Integrity value recorded per package entry, against which `npm ci` verifies each fetched tarball; it is the only artifact-level guarantee in the supply chain (§3.3.2) |
| Nested copy | A package installed below another rather than hoisted, because the requirement cannot be satisfied by the top-level version: `node_modules/type-is/node_modules/content-type` at 2.0.0 alongside top-level `content-type` at 1.0.5 (§3.3.2) |
| Peer, optional and development dependencies | Dependency classes that would attach tooling to the build. All three are absent: no entry is marked optional, none declares a peer requirement, and no development package exists (§3.3.2) |
| Placeholder test script | The untouched `npm init` value in `package.json#scripts.test`, `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`. It fails by design and therefore guards nothing (§3.6.1, §6.6.3.3) |
| CommonJS module without exports | The module shape of `server.js`: `require` at the top, no `module.exports` anywhere. Requiring the file therefore starts a listener and yields an empty export object, which is why handler-level unit testing is unavailable without a source change (§3.1.2, §6.6.2.1) |
| Module cache | The runtime's loaded-module registry, in which `express` and its 65 transitives appear once per process, loaded at startup rather than per request (§4.3.1.1) |

### 9.2.4 Repository, Artifact and Fixture Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|------|------------------------------------------|
| Tracked file | A path recorded in git. The repository has 19, and `node_modules/` is deliberately not among them (§9.1.1) |
| Git-ignored | Excluded by a `.gitignore` rule. The file holds one rule, `node_modules/`, whose effect is that installation is a precondition of running and the repository stays source-only (§3.6.6) |
| Working tree | The checkout's uncommitted state. It is clean at HEAD, so the committed bytes and the files on disk agree (§3.6.6) |
| Commit, base commit and HEAD | The 11 commits on the single branch; the base `46e6dfe` that carried the pre-Express assets; and HEAD `fdeac01`, four documentation commits beyond the last code change (§9.1.3) |
| Fixture | Used in two senses. A **filename fixture** is one of the three byte-identical native-`http` scripts kept for their pathological names (F-009). A **data fixture** is `phonenumber.csv`, carried with no consumer (F-010). Neither is a test fixture in the testing sense, since no test framework exists (§2.1.3.9, §2.1.3.10) |
| Pathological filename | A deliberately hostile file name used to exercise tooling that ingests the repository: a double dot inside the basename (`Test.test..js`), shell metacharacters (`!@#$%^&().js`), and a 199-character name (§2.1.3.9, §9.1.1) |
| Orphan fixture | A committed file no code path reads. `phonenumber.csv` is the only data file of this kind; its schema is defined solely by its own header, `message,phonenumber` (§9.1.5) |
| Unreferenced or dormant artifact | A tracked file that participates in no build, run or verification step: the four binaries and the orphan CSV, which together are 90.9% of tracked bytes (§9.1.5, §9.1.7) |
| Binary artifact | A non-text tracked file with no language and no runtime role — a PDF, an OOXML document, a PNG and an MP4 (§3.1.1, §9.1.5) |
| Prose artifact | Markdown or JSON-wrapped Markdown carrying requirements, validation evidence or operational guidance rather than executable behaviour; it is the source of every requirement ID this specification cites (§9.1.2) |
| Documentation set | The four Markdown artifacts under `blitzy/documentation/` — action plan, build prompt, project guide and technical specifications — none of which is read by executing code (§5.1.2, component C-8) |
| Digest | A cryptographic hash of file bytes used to identify an artifact. This document records MD5 values for the four JavaScript files (§2.5.3, §6.6.7.4) and SHA-256 values for all 19 tracked paths (§9.1.1); they are different digests of the same bytes, not competing records |
| Byte count versus character count | Different measures of the same file. `blitzy/documentation/Build Prompt.md` is 214 bytes but 210 characters, because its curly quotation marks occupy three bytes each in UTF-8; §9.1.2 therefore states which measure each figure uses |
| Mermaid diagram source | Fenced `mermaid` blocks embedded in Markdown and rendered by tooling, not by the service. The superseded specification carries 47 of them and the project guide 3 (§9.1.2) |

## 9.4 References

#### Files Examined

- `server.js` — The only runtime module (28 lines, 870 bytes, SHA-256 `a9a9b304…`): `require('express')`, hostname and port literals, `express()`, `app.enable('strict routing')`, the two `GET` registrations with their byte-exact bodies, and the `app.listen` callback emitting the startup line. Source of every contract statement in §9.1 and §9.2.
- `package.json` — Package identity (`hello_world` v1.0.0, MIT, author `hxu`), the single `express ^5.2.1` dependency, the absent `engines` field, the `main` reference to a non-existent `index.js`, and the placeholder `test` script.
- `package-lock.json` — `lockfileVersion` 3 with 67 `packages` keys (root plus 66 packages), each pinned by version, registry URL and `sha512` digest; basis of §9.2.3's dependency definitions.
- `.gitignore` — Single rule `node_modules/` (14 bytes), which makes installation a precondition of running and keeps the repository source-only.
- `README.md` — Identity line, both endpoints with their status, content type and bodies, the `404` behaviour, and the `npm install` / `node server.js` run procedure; the published contract that serves as the verification oracle.
- `Test.test..js`, `!@#$%^&().js`, `QWYFFGHGHFDDJFDame_!@#$%^&(){}long_name_…_server.js` — Three byte-identical native-`http` fixtures (14 lines, 342 bytes, SHA-256 `332fc2d0…`), with 13-, 12- and 199-character names; established their continued divergence from `server.js` and fixed the filename length recorded in §9.1.6.
- `phonenumber.csv` — Header `message,phonenumber` plus 15 synthetic rows, read by no code path; schema and role recorded in §9.1.5.
- `codebase_context (42).md` — Original single-line requirement note asking for one `/hello` endpoint returning `"Hello world"`; the unmet requirement F-201.
- `Response.txt` — JSON envelope (51 lines, 35,535 bytes) whose `sections[0].content` payload carries the §0.1–§0.7 hardening plan: definitions of F-101–F-106, their change blocks, and the aspirational thresholds quoted in §5.4.5.
- `blitzy/documentation/Agent Action Plan.md` — Requirement IDs FR-A–FR-D, the verbatim prompt, the scope inventory and exclusions, and the Express 5 / Node.js 18+ research record.
- `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` — Completion and hour breakdown, the 15-check validation register, runtime validation results, compliance mapping, risk register, development guide, and the appendices that first recorded a glossary and command reference for this repository.
- `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` — The superseded specification of the pre-Express state, including its own feature catalogue, workflows W-01–W-09, and the freshness note that any change to `server.js` invalidates its criteria.
- `blitzy/documentation/Build Prompt.md` — The requester's prompt (single unterminated line, 214 bytes / 210 characters), the origin of the delivered feature.
- `tech_spec.pdf`, `defect_for_task_1.docx`, `s1.png`, `20250304165759.mp4` — The four unreferenced binaries; measured properties recorded in §9.1.5 (PDF 1.7, OOXML package with a 111-character body text and two embedded images, PNG 1152 × 958, MP4 brand `mp42`).

#### Folders Examined

- Repository root (depth 0) — 15 tracked paths plus `.git` and the ignored `node_modules/`; the complete file and folder census in §9.1.1 and §9.1.7 was taken here.
- `blitzy/` (depth 1) — Contains only the `documentation` subtree; no code or configuration.
- `blitzy/documentation/` (depth 2) — The four tracked Markdown artifacts inventoried in §9.1.2; no executables.
- `node_modules/` (depth 1–3) — 65 top-level package directories plus the nested `type-is/node_modules/content-type`, 4.2 MB in total, no `.bin` directory; confirmed the installed tree matches the lockfile entry for entry.

#### Runtime and Repository Evidence

Collected at HEAD `fdeac01eb92db36b932a03c0065b5644e250fbe0` on branch `blitzy-62d685d6-e32c-4f29-bfd6-70d96dfe345a` with Node.js v22.23.3 and npm 11.21.0, leaving the working tree clean:

- `git ls-files`, `git log --pretty` and `git show --stat` — established the 19 tracked paths, the 11-commit history with authors and per-commit line statistics, the base commit `46e6dfe`, and the `.gitignore` and lockfile provenance recorded in §9.1.3.
- `sha256sum`, `md5sum`, `wc -l`, `wc -c`, `stat` and a filename-length enumeration — produced every size, digest and line count in §9.1.1, §9.1.2 and §9.1.6, including the 7,147,208 tracked bytes and the 6,498,983 binary bytes.
- `du -sh node_modules/` and directory listings at depth 1 and 3 — established the 4.2 MB dependency tree, its 66 packages and the nested `content-type` copy.
- OOXML and PDF inspection with Python's `zipfile` and `zlib` — extracted the 111-character body text and the two embedded images from `defect_for_task_1.docx`, and established that `tech_spec.pdf` is a PDF 1.7 file with compressed object streams whose page count could not be re-derived from the byte stream.
